definition: Object detection is a computer technology related to computer vision and image processing that deals with detecting instances of semantic objects of a certain class (such as humans, buildings, or cars) in digital images and videos.
details: Well-researched domains of object detection include face detection and pedestrian detection. Object detection has applications in many areas of computer vision, including image retrieval and video surveillance.

explainer.lead: Object detection finds instances of semantic object classes, such as humans, buildings or cars, in digital images and videos. It matters because it locates objects and names them, supporting retrieval and surveillance.

tiers.eli5: It draws a box around every car or person it finds in a picture and says what each box contains.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train detectors on labelled boxes for classes like faces or pedestrians; a common pitfall is that performance on one well-studied domain does not transfer unchanged to another.
tiers.paperLevel: Given an image, output a set of bounding boxes each with a class label for instances of the target classes; well-researched domains include face and pedestrian detection, and results depend on the classes and data used.

explainer.example: A video frame is processed and the system returns boxes labelled 'person' and 'car' with positions.
